info.bio: Sasha comenzó su carrera como disc jockey de música del género acid house a finales de la década de 1980. Desde entonces comenzó a ser popular en el ámbito de la música dance. En 1995 comenzó a hacer dueto con el DJ John Digweed con quien ha hecho varias giras internacionales y varios álbumes. Sasha y Digweed han sido muy importantes en la evolución del trance progresivo y el house en todos sus géneros. Sasha ha producido varios éxitos en el Reino Unido y ha hecho remixes de artistas como "Madonna" y "The chemical Brothers".

podcast.title: Early Screamo Influence
podcast.body: Sasha was one of the bands mentioned by Dallas Green as an influence for the early "screamo" sound that helped inform Alexis on Fire's distinct style, part of a collection of lesser-known acts that band members sought out in their youth. "I was kind of more the deep head early first-screamo stuff like where I was listening to bands like Sasha, Love Lost, Penoffa, Godden, these are all different."

xref.body: Dave Navarro, known for his work with Jane's Addiction, wrote and directed a porn film titled "Broken" for Evan Seinfeld and Tara Patrick's company, starring Sasha Grey. While he did not perform in any X-rated scenes, he expressed enjoyment for the line of work. In 2014, he collaborated with BDSM company The Stock Room to design a guitar strap that could also function as a multi-purpose BDSM restraint and sex sling. "Dave Navarro, best known for his work with James Diction, wrote and directed a porn film entitled Broken for Evan and Tara's Company."

xref.title: Early Screamo Influence
xref.body: Love Lost was cited by Dallas Green as an influence on the early "screamo" sound that shaped Alexis on Fire's music. This was part of a specific subgenre of aggressive music that required active searching to discover, often through vinyl distros at local shows. "I was kind of more the deep head early first-screamo stuff like where I was listening to bands like Sasha, Love Lost, Penoffa, Godden, these are all different."

xref.title: Influences: Screamo, Melodic Hardcore, and Converge
xref.body: At the time of the band's formation (2000–2001), emo was not a mainstream genre. Their influences included melodic hardcore, early screamo (bands such as Sasha and Page 99), hardcore, and post-hardcore. Converge was a shared influence among members. "At their formation, 'emo' was not a mainstream genre; their influences included melodic hardcore, early screamo, and Converge."
